'''Ante Toni Žižić''' ({{IPA|hr|antɛ ʐǐːʐitɕ}}; born 4 January 1997) is a Croatian professional [[basketball]] player for [[Beşiktaş J.K. (men's basketball)|Beşiktaş]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL). He was selected 23rd overall by the [[Boston Celtics]] in the [[2016 NBA draft]]. He played in the [[2018 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]] as a member of the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in 2018.

==Professional career==
===Kaštela (2013–2014)===
Žižić's first team was [[KK Split]], in the 2013–14 season, but he played for their junior team, in which he only played in 3 games. He then moved to the [[Cedevita Zagreb]]'s junior team, and with them he played in 5 games.

===Gorica (2014)===
To start the 2014–15 season, Žižić played for [[KK Gorica|Gorica]].

===Cibona (2014–2016)===
Žižiće moved to [[Cibona Zagreb]] for the rest of the season. In that year, he averaged 7.4 points, 0.3 assists, 0.3 steals, and 0.9 blocks, in 15.5 minutes per game, in 25 games played in the [[Adriatic League]]. His breakout season was in the 2015–16 season.

He was named the [[2015–16 ABA League]] season's [[ABA League Top Prospect|top prospect]]. In that season, he averaged 12.7 points, 7.2 rebounds, and 1.2 blocks in 24.8 minutes per game, in 26 games played in the Adriatic League.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aba-liga.com/news/tabid/86/id/36359/201516-top-prospect-ante-ii.aspx |title=2015/16 Top Prospect: Ante Žižić |work=ABA-Liga.com |date=9 March 2016 |access-date=9 March 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160309215453/http://aba-liga.com/news/tabid/86/id/36359/201516-top-prospect-ante-ii.aspx |archive-date=9 March 2016 }}</ref> He was also named to the [[European professional club basketball system|European-wide 3rd-tier-level]] [[FIBA Europe Cup]]'s Starting Five Team of the [[2015–16 FIBA Europe Cup|2015–16 season]].{{fact|date=June 2026}}

On 11 October 2016, Žižić was named the MVP of the fourth week of the [[2016–17 ABA League]] season. He scored 37 points and grabbed 20 rebounds in Cibona's 89–85 win over [[MZT Skopje Aerodrom]], in a game that was decided after double [[overtime (sports)|overtime]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aba-liga.com/news.php?id=37058|title=Round 4 MVP: Ante Žižić (Cibona)|work=ABA-Liga.com|date=11 October 2016|access-date=11 October 2016}}</ref>

===Darüşşafaka (2016–2017)===
On 27 December 2016, Žižić left Cibona, and signed with the Turkish team [[Darüşşafaka Doğuş]], of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi|Turkish Super League]].<ref>{{cite news |date=27 December 2016 |title=Darussafaka Dogus signs Ante Zizic |work=Sportando.com |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/221472/darussafaka-dogus-signs-ante-zizic.html |url-status=dead |access-date=27 December 2016 |archive-date=28 December 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161228033113/http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/221472/darussafaka-dogus-signs-ante-zizic.html }}</ref>

With Darüşşafaka, Žižić made his debut in the [[European professional club basketball system|European top-tier level]], the [[EuroLeague]], on 30 December 2016, in an 81–77 road loss against [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]]. In his first EuroLeague game, Žižić had 4 points, 6 rebounds, 2 steals, and 2 blocks.<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=118&seasoncode=E2016#!boxscore FC BARCELONA LASSA 81 DARUSSAFAKA DOGUS ISTANBUL 77 DECEMBER 30, 2016.]</ref>

===Cleveland Cavaliers (2017–2020)===
[[File:Ante Žižić - Cleveland Cavaliers vs. Brooklyn Nets (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|Žižić with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in 2019]]
Žižić was selected with the 23rd overall pick in the [[2016 NBA draft]], by the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Hutchinson |first=Kara |date=24 June 2016 |title=Boston Celtics 2016 Draft Results |work=NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/boston-celtics-2016-draft-results |access-date=28 July 2016}}</ref>

On 1 July 2017, Žižić signed with the Boston Celtics.<ref>{{cite news|title=Celtics Sign Jayson Tatum, Ante Zizic|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-sign-jayson-tatum-ante-zizic|access-date=1 July 2017|work=NBA.com|date=1 July 2017}}</ref> Before even suiting up for a single regular-season game for the Celtics, Žižić was traded to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] alongside [[Isaiah Thomas (basketball)|Isaiah Thomas]], [[Jae Crowder]], and the [[Brooklyn Nets]]' unprotected [[2018 NBA draft|2018 first-round pick]] for [[Kyrie Irving]] on 22 August 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-acquire-four-time-all-star-kyrie-irving|title=Celtics Acquire Four-Time All-Star Kyrie Irving|work=NBA.com|date=22 August 2017|access-date=22 August 2017}}</ref> However, eight days after the trade was first confirmed, the Celtics would also add a [[2020 NBA draft|2020 second-round pick]] from the [[Miami Heat]] in order to fully complete the deal to satisfy Cleveland's worries involving Thomas's hip injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ellentuck |first=Matt |date=30 August 2017 |title=Kyrie Irving trade finalized with Celtics adding 2020 2nd-round pick |url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2017/8/30/16224168/kyrie-irving-trade-to-celtics-finalized-with-boston-adding-2020-second-round-pick |access-date=8 August 2023 |website=sbnation.com}}</ref>

Žižić spent time with the [[Canton Charge]] during his rookie season. On 11 March, he scored 15 points and recorded 7 rebounds (both career highs) in a loss to the [[2017–18 Los Angeles Lakers season|Los Angeles Lakers]]. In the last game of the regular season, he scored 20 points and recorded 7 rebounds. The Cavaliers made it to the [[2018 NBA Finals]], but lost the series 4–0 to the [[2017–18 Golden State Warriors season|Golden State Warriors]].

===Maccabi Tel Aviv (2020–2022)===
On 25 August 2020, Žižić signed a two-year deal with Israeli team [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Maggi |first=Alessandro |date=25 August 2020 |title=Ante Zizic is officially a newcomer of Maccabi Tel Aviv |website=Sportando |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/ante-zizic-is-officially-a-newcomer-of-maccabi-tel-aviv/ |access-date=25 August 2020}}</ref> In 2020–21, he led the league with a .699 field goal percentage, and was 10th in the Euroleague with 0.8 blocks per game.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/international/israel-super-league/2021.html|title = Israeli Super League - 2020-21 Standings and Stats}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/league/1/Euroleague/stats/2021/Averages/Qualified/All/blocks/All/desc|title = Euroleague Stats - RealGM}}</ref>

On 9 May 2022, during a game against [[Hapoel Haifa B.C.|Hapoel Haifa]], Žižić lost consciousness after hitting his head on the ground. He was rushed to a hospital and regained consciousness later that night.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Askounis |first=Johnny |date=9 May 2022 |title=Ante Zizic rushed to the hospital after a head injury |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/others/1343636/ante-zizic-suffers-scary-head-injury/ |access-date=12 May 2022 |website=Eurohoops}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Gaydos |first=Ryan |date=10 May 2022 |title=Ex-NBA first-round pick suffers head injury after scary fall in Israeli basketball game, sends fans message |url=https://www.foxnews.com/sports/nba-first-round-pick-head-injury-fall-israeli-basketball-game |access-date=12 May 2022 |website=Fox News}}</ref>

On 21 June 2022, Žižić officially parted ways with the Israeli club after two seasons.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/ante-zizic-officially-leaves-maccabi-tel-aviv/|title=Ante Zizic officially leaves Maccabi Tel Aviv|date=21 June 2022|website=|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=21 June 2022|last=Maggi |first=Alessandro }}</ref>

===Anadolu Efes (2022–2023)===
On 22 June 2022, Žižić signed a three-year (2+1) contract with Turkish club [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]], the reigning back-to-back [[EuroLeague]] champions.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://anadoluefessk.org/haber/ante-zizic-anadolu-efes-te|title=Ante Zizic Anadolu Efes'te|last=|first=|date=22 June 2022|website=|publisher=[[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]]|language=tr|access-date=1 July 2022}}</ref>

===Virtus Bologna (2023–2025)===
On 31 December 2023, Žižić signed a two-year contract with Italian powerhouse [[Virtus Bologna]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-12-31 |title=Ante Žižić is a new player of Virtus Segafredo Bologna!
|url=https://www.virtus.it/en/news/ante-zizic-is-a-new-player-of-virtus-segafredo-bologna/ |language=en-US}}</ref> Despite an impressive first half of the season, Virtus ended the EuroLeague regular season at the 10th place, qualifying only for the [[2023–24 EuroLeague#Play-in|play-in]], where after having defeated 67–64 [[Anadolu Efes]], it lost against [[Saski Baskonia|Baskonia]] 89–77, not qualifying for the playoffs.<ref>[https://www.rainews.it/tgr/emiliaromagna/articoli/2024/04/la-virtus-perde-lo-spareggio-con-il-baskonia-ed-e-decima-908bfb4e-0b89-4ece-879a-08b52af05723.html Basket, la Virtus perde lo spareggio con il Baskonia ed è decima]. Rai News</ref> Moreover, the Black V placed first during the Italian regular season but, after having knocked out [[Derthona Basket|Tortona]] by 3–2 and [[Reyer Venezia]] by 3–1, it lost the third consecutive final against Milan by 3–1.<ref>[https://www.eurosport.it/basket/serie-a/2023-2024/lolimpia-milano-chiude-sul-3-1-le-finali-con-la-virtus-bologna-e-il-terzo-scudetto-consecutivo-il-31o-della-storia_sto20010851/story.shtml L'Olimpia Milano chiude sul 3-1 le finali con la Virtus Bologna, è il terzo scudetto consevutivo e il 31° della storia]. EuroSport</ref>

In the following season Virtus ended the EuroLeague at the 17th place, after a disappointing regular season. After arriving first in the national championship season, Virtus eliminated Venezia 3–2 and their arch-rival Milan 3–1, reaching their fifth finals in a row. They then defeated Brescia 3–0, claiming the Italian championship title for the 17th time.<ref>[https://sport.sky.it/basket/serie-a/2025/06/17/brescia-virtus-bologna-gara-3-risultato La Virtus Bologna vince il suo 17° scudetto: 3-0 a Brescia in finale playoff]. Sky Sport</ref><ref>[https://www.ilpost.it/2025/06/17/virtus-bologna-scudetto-serie-a-basket-2025/ La Virtus Bologna ha vinto la Serie A di basket]. Il Post</ref>

===Beşiktaş (2025–present)===
On 1 July 2025, Žižić signed with [[Beşiktaş J.K. (men's basketball)|Beşiktaş Gain]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bjk.com.tr/tr/haber/91979/ante-zizic-besiktas-gainde.html |title=Ante Zizic Beşiktaş GAİN’de|language=tr|date=2025-07-10|access-date=2025-07-12}}</ref> On 7 June 2026, it was announced that Žižić would require surgery to repair an [[acromioclavicular joint|AC joint]] injury in his left shoulder.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Besiktas big man Ante Žižić to undergo surgery|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/tbl/1977547/ante-zizic-to-undergo-surgery/|access-date=July 4, 2026|website=eurohoops.net|language=en}}</ref>

==National team career==
Žižić played with the junior national teams of Croatia. With Croatia's junior national teams, he played at the [[2013 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]], the [[2014 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]], where he won a bronze medal, and at the [[2015 FIBA Under-19 World Championship]], where he won a silver medal.

==Personal life==
[[File:Ante Zizic.jpg|thumb|upright|Žižić at an U16 tournament in 2013]]
Žižić's older brother, [[Andrija Žižić|Andrija]], is a former professional [[basketball]] player. The two brothers were teammates at [[Cibona Zagreb]] during the 2015–16 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://slobodnadalmacija.hr/Ko%C5%A1arka/tabid/85/articleType/ArticleView/articleId/209769/Default.aspx|title=Brother vs. Brother, Andrija vs. Ante|language=hr|date=10 May 2013|publisher=Slobodna Dalmacija}}</ref> His older brother played in 107 [[EuroLeague]] games with Cibona Zagreb, [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]], [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]] and [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]], and he also won a EuroLeague championship with [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]].
